Bielema played in the 1991 Rose Bowl as an Iowa defensive lineman, though the Hawkeyes took a 46-34 loss to Washington. Bielema gave his father, Arnie, his Rose Bowl watch he earned from that game, and his father wore that watch until his death last month. Bret Bielema wore that watch all of last week leading into Friday's 24-13 win over Nebraska — on Dad's Day at the university. As a coach, Bielema then led Wisconsin to three straight Rose Bowl Games, coaching them in two (211 and 2012) before leaving the Badgers for Arkansas before the 2013 Rose Bowl Game. Before this trip to Pasadena to play No. 4 UCLA , Bielema made sure to remind his players — or teach them — the history behind the Bruins' home venue. "To have this moment, I'm going to show the guys a video [on Monday] because I'm making a really big deal about playing in the Rose Bowl, how awesome this is," Bielema said. Oh, and this game against a top-five opponent gives the rejuvenated Fighting Illini a chance to really push its midseason turnaround to another tier. Illinois (6-3, 4-2 Big Ten) has won four straight games to clinch a bowl bid, something that seemed unlikely following a 2-3 start and blowing a 16-point second-half lead at Michigan State and losing starting quarterback Katin Houser to a hand injury before pulling out a 38-37 win overtime. Now, Illinois faces one of its toughest tasks of the season against the Bruins (9-0, 6-0 Big Ten), who have gone from bottom of the Big Ten to the conference's top-ranked team under first-year head coach Bob Chesney . But Friday's 8 p.m. CT kickoff (FOX) also gives the Illini a massive opportunity. "These moments, these opportunities don't come about very often," Bielema said. "Obviously to play in the Rose Bowl is a whole huge deal. I kind of made an important point to them all year, but to play a team of this caliber who's undefeated in Game 10 is just absolutely awesome. So I think our guys are excited for the moment." A win at a top-10 team would give Illinois, which beat No. 18 Oregon two weeks ago, the type of win that makes the College Football Playoff committee take them seriously entering the final two weeks of the season. "The opportunity obviously to go play a nationally ranked undefeated team at their home spot, it'l be a tremendous challenge. We're going to have to play extremely well," Illinois offensive coordinator Barry Lunney Jr. said. "But one of the things about fun about college football is the opportunity to make memories and certainly we have that opportunity on Friday." away.headline: Illinois Star David Mirkovic Takes Big Step Toward Return
away.blurb: Illinois Star David Mirkovic Takes Big Step Toward Return IllinoisRoundtable 41 Members • 546 Posts IllinoisRoundtable IllinoisRoundtable Related stories Credit: Bob Donnan-Imagn Images Credit: Bob Donnan-Imagn Images Illinois Star David Mirkovic Takes Big Step Toward Return Ezra Lombardi Partner Nov 13, 2026 4:01 PM Published Nov 13, 2026 4:01 PM Illinois head coach Brad Underwood provided some encouraging updates on David Mirkovic as he works back from both foot and appendix surgery. Mirkovic, who has been spotted out of the walking boot, is "starting his process" to ramp back up after the appendix surgery. Underwood explained that after a follow-up appointment on Thursday, he would begin the "procedure process" needed to get comfortable post-op. The 2-1 Illinois men's basketball team came into the season without star forward David Mirkovic. His absence was expected, as the sophomore underwent foot surgery in August which put him on a scooter and in a walking boot for several months. What was not expected was the emergency appendectomy that he required just days before the season opener. The additional procedure obviously put his status in question beyond the health of his foot with the standard recovery time from appendix surgery set around six weeks. But at practice on Thursday ahead of the Fighting Illini's matchup with 2-1 Sam Houston, head coach Brad Underwood gave an encouraging update on Mirkovic regarding both the foot and the stomach. Most notably, Underwood said that Mirkovic is shooting a basketball again, which he called a good sign that "his stomach is in an okay spot where it's not too painful." The tandem rehab of foot and appendix is a complicated one. With the foot still not 100 percent, it will be difficult to get the conditioning drills in that are necessary to test the strength of the midsection. At the same time, the training staff likely won't want to push it too hard on the appendix just yet, which could potential slow the strengthening exercises for his foot. That said, it's promising to see Mirkovic take these steps forward now a few months removed from foot surgery but just under two weeks from the appendectomy. Underwood did clarify over a week ago that Mirkovic had undergone laparoscopic surgery, which presents several advantages over the traditional open appendectomy. With this, he should experience a quicker recovery and less pain in the early postoperative stages. The update here seemingly confirms this to a certain extent, with Mirkovic able to manage the pain enough to get shots up so soon after the surgery. The absence of Mirkovic has already been felt by the Illini. After losing fellow starter Jake Davis to shoulder surgery , Illinois dropped an early game to Texas Tech in Lubbock by a score of 84-78. Getting Mirkovic back in the mix should help prevent similar setbacks for a team with real title aspirations.

picks.blurb: 2026 Week 11 Preview: Wake Forest Demon Deacons @ SMU Mustangs | Underdog Dynasty Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Rest of the FBS Community Underdog Dynasty November 13, 2026 Underdog Dynasty Notifications Notifications The Feed Sections Conference USA Sun Belt Conference American Athletic Conference Betting FanDuel College Football Odds College Football Picks and Predictions Community Guidelines Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Sections Expand Conference USA Betting Expand FanDuel College Football Odds All communities Notifications ACC Wake Forest is rolling toward the ACC title game. But SMU, which has never lost a home ACC game, can stay in the race. Time and date: Saturday, November 14 at 12:00 p.m. ET Network: ESPN Location: Gerald J. Ford Stadium — Dallas, TX Spread: SMU (-1.5) Over/under: 61.5 All-time series: SMU leads, 3-1 Last meeting: Wake Forest 13, SMU 12 — October 25, 2025 Current streak: Wake Forest, 1 (2025) Setting the scene This might be the ACC regular season game of the year. For the first time in College Football Playoff history, the ACC champion is guaranteed an automatic bid. Thus, just getting access to Charlotte keeps the door ajar for Wake Forest and SMU in this high-stakes conference showdown. The Demon Deacons are one of the hottest teams in college football, winning six consecutive games, primarily in blowout fashion. But the Mustangs haven’t ever lost an matchup at Gerald J. Ford Stadium, faring 12-0 in their previous contests. A Wake Forest win propels the Demon Deacons to the doorstep of the ACC Championship Game. An SMU win creates chaos, bringing a cluster of 2-loss teams back into championship consideration, including itself. The ACC races greatly hinges on what unfolds Saturday afternoon on The Hilltop. Wake Forest Demon Deacons outlook Wake Forest (8-1, 5-1 ACC) is ranked No. 13 by the College Football Playoff committee, situated as the second-highest ACC team. Since its lone September loss to Miami (FL), the Demon Deacons have been as dominant as anyone in the FBS. During the last five games of its six-game win streak, Wake Forest has defeated opponents by an aggregate score of 264-31, or an average of 53-6 per game. The Demon Deacons used a dominant defense to stun SMU 13-12 in last year’s meeting in Winston-Salem, but this season, the offense has hit its stride under second-year coordinator Rob Ezell. Wake Forest ranks fourth nationally in scoring (43.3 points per game), ninth in total offense, and 10th in passing. Starting quarterback Gio Lopez missed last week’s game against FCS Merrimack with a lower body injury, but the absence was permissible due to the level of opponent. The former South Alabama and North Carolina gunslinger has been phenomenal in his new home, delivering 18 touchdowns against one interception this year, ranking 13th nationally in passing average. His mobility has made defenses pay too, accumulating 317 rushing yards and six touchdowns on the season. Lopez’s top target Carlos Hernandez is receiving national recognition. The senior is sixth in the FBS with an average of 105 receiving yards per game, and he regularly strikes from distance. Hernandez has multiple 70-yard touchdowns this season, and he has four outings with at least 110 yards and an end zone appearance. Jack Foley, Kam Shanks, and Antonio Meeks have provided support in this dynamic aerial attack, and the diversity in options allows Wake Forest to have the nation’s ninth-most efficient third down offense. The run game has been serviceable, ranking 43rd nationally in yards per game, while producing 4.94 yards per carry. Ty Clark and Deuce Lawrence have split carries throughout the season, totaling 416 and 327 rushing yards, respectively. Wake Forest’s offensive improvement has somewhat obscured the consistent impact of its defense. The Demon Deacons have only surrendered multiple scores once in their past five games, and they’ve finished 22 consecutive quarters without allowing more than seven points. The result is the country’s 13th-ranked scoring defense and 24th-ranked total defense — a unit which is particularly stingent against the run, surrendering just 85 yards per game on a 2.69 average. Defensive end Langston Hardy is the leader of the run-stuffing effort. He leads all ACC players with 13.5 tackles for loss, while also producing 44 tackles and 5.5 sacks. Backfield pressure has been a signature of this Wake Forest defense, and two other defensive linemen — Gabe Kirschke and Zach Lohavichan — have at least 7.5 tackles for loss. Wake Forest’s defense found the sustainable method of success, and that’s getting stops. The Demon Deacons are fifth nationally in both red zone defense and fourth down defense, finding ways to get off the field in critical situations. The unit can become even more dangerous if it dabbles in the turnover game. Wake Forest has forced just seven takeaways all season, which is tied for the eighth-fewest in the FBS. SMU Mustangs outlook SMU (7-2, 5-2 ACC) prepares for a revenge game against Wake Forest. Had the Mustangs prevailed last October in Winston-Salem, they would have competed in the ACC Championship Game with a College Football Playoff spot on the line. Instead, they fell in a 13-12 heartbreaker on a last-second field goal — one of the program’s four ACC losses since joining the conference in 2024. Zero of those losses transpired at Gerald J. Ford Stadium. SMU has been a different beast at home, and that was evident in its most complete game of the season last Friday against Virginia Tech. Counting games against FBS opponents, the Mustangs registered a season-high 23 first half points, utilizing its strongest start of the season to push past the Hokies, 51-28. The concept of senior day might have lost some luster in the transfer portal era, but Saturday will feature one of the most emotional senior day moments in recent memory. Kevin Jennings is in his fifth year with the program and third as the starting quarterback, and the Dallas area native has poured a lot into the program. Jennings guided the Mustangs to an American Conference title, an ACC Championship Game appearance, a College Football Playoff berth, and a Holiday Bowl victory. Now he’ll play his final game in Dallas, entering the pivotal matchup fifth nationally with 2,764 passing yards and fourth with 25 touchdown passes. The most remarkable part of Jennings’ eye-popping stats is his efficiency. For a quarterback that slings it deep quite often, the senior boasts a 73.9 completion rate, which is second among all players with at least 100 attempts. Jennings has also limited interceptions this year, finishing four of his last five starts without one. SMU’s high-powered passing attack involves a slew of receivers. Yamir Knight, coming off a 103-yard, 3-touchdown performance, is the most frequented with a team-high 50 catches. But Yannick Smith, Jalen Cooper, and Jalen Hale are also heavily involved — especially on downfield attempts — and all three average over 15.0 yards per reception this season. Tight ends Randy Pittman Jr. and Theo Melin Öhrström are also regular targets, tied for second on the team with four touchdown receptions apiece. The Mustangs’ run game is statistically a middle-of-the-road unit, ranked 70th in yards per game and 66th in rushing average. Kendrick Raphael operates as the top option, and he’s scored in seven of nine contests this year. Freshman Christian Rhodes has seen an increasing number of reps since mid-October, and he’s coming off a career-high 92 rushing yards against Virginia Tech. On defense, SMU displays a similar identity to the previous Mustang defenses of the Rhett Lashlee era: defensive line dominance. The Mustangs are one of 17 programs racking up at least 3.0 sacks per game, and defensive end Marques White is the ringleader of the movement. The eighth-year senior notched his third multi-sack game of the season last week, contributing to the turnover battle with a forced fumble and fumble recovery on the same play. But unlike the previous two seasons, SMU isn’t collecting turnovers on a consistent basis. The Mustangs have forced just eight turnovers all year, recovering five fumbles and picking off two passes. Despite the lack of takeaways, the secondary has shown considerable improvement from 2025, skyrocketing from 135th to 42nd in passing yards allowed per game, with safeties Jimmy Wyrick and Sael Reyes playing significant roles in that progress. Last year’s matchup between SMU and Wake Forest was the ultimate defensive battle. Just two touchdowns were scored — one on a 14-play drive and another capping a 41-yard series. There were eight combined turnovers in the matchup, which was decided on Connor Calvert’s 50-yard field goal as time expired. This year’s rematch looks bound to lean more on the higher-scoring end. Wake Forest brings significantly more offensive firepower in this matchup, headlined by the strong connection between Gio Lopez and Carlos Hernandez. The Demon Deacons’ offense has been virtually unstoppable since the start of October, and while SMU should provide some resistance with a formidable defensive line, Wake Forest will still get its points in Dallas. However, SMU can thrive in a shootout style game. The Mustangs are one of the most explosive offenses in the country, ranking ninth in the FBS with 15 plays spanning 40 yards. Wake Forest has excelled at preventing the big play this year, but the Mustangs’ receiving corps should present challenges on the back end that the Demon Deacons haven’t seen since the Miami (FL) loss. This back-and-forth thriller will come down to crunch time. With the backing of its home crowd, SMU improves to 13-0 in ACC matchups at Gerald J. Ford Stadium — a result which will add significant chaos to the final two weeks of ACC play. Wake Forest is one of the hottest teams college football right now, putting together an impressive five-game winning streak to improve to 7-1 overall and 5-1 in ACC play. The Demon Deacons first edged out then-No. 16 Louisville 30-27 on the road on Sept. 26 before blowing Stanford 57-3 at home, NC State (38-14) and Cal (41-7) both on the road, and then knocking off Virginia 51-7 last weekend. However, Wake Forest could be without its starting quarterback for Saturday's home matchup against Merrimack. Lopez suffered a lower-body injury during last weekend's rout of Virginia, forcing him to leave the game late in the third quarter. He was described as day-to-day earlier in the week, but ESPN's Pete Thamel reported Saturday morning that the team will start Steele Pizzella against Merrimack instead, holding Lopez out as a precaution, and that he should be back against SMU next week. The ACC's top two teams will meet in the conference championship game on Dec. 5, with the winner receiving an automatic playoff berth. Wake currently sits behind Miami for second place in the conference, but SMU is right behind them at 7-2. The Demon Deacons will face the Mustangs next weekend in Dallas, a game that's setting up to be massive for both sides. After that, Wake Forest will go on the road to face Georgia Tech and then close things out back home against Duke. It's official: Poch to Man United Sportscaster Dan Hicks dies ESPN FPI predicts Texas A&M vs. No. 13 Tennessee in Week 11 Cameron Ohnysty, Aggies Wire · Aggies Wire Mon, November 9, 2026 at 10:31 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Despite two full weeks of rest during the bye week, Texas A&M fell to 4-4 and 1-5 in SEC play after losing to South Carolina on the road, once again failing to close out the game after holding a lead into the fourth quarter. Again, Texas A&M is a bad football team with way more questions than answers, and with three games remaining, the pressure continues to mount on third-year coach Mike Elko . Will the coaching staff change during the season? That remains to be seen, and after making his ninth start, senior quarterback Marcel Reed isn't expected to be benched. While Reed played better, completing 25-of-43 for 251 yards, Texas A&M failed to score a touchdown for the third time in SEC play, and is reportedly the first team to produce over 450 yards without a touchdown, adding more insult to injury to a season that has been lost for quite some time. Set to return to Kyle Field for the second-to-last time this season, Texas A&M will host No. 13 Tennessee and is currently a 3.5-point home underdog, which isn't surprising, especially after watching the Volunteers blow out Kentucky 34-6 behind 240 rushing yards. Per ESPN FPI, Tennessee has a 58.6% chance to defeat Texas A&M (41.4%) after the Aggies were favored pre-season and for most of the regular season. Tennessee's defense should be able to eliminate explosive plays, and after watching Texas A&M's offensive line break down in pass protection late in the game, the Volunteers' pass rush should have zero issues. Texas A&M will host Tennessee on Saturday, November 14, at 2:00 p.m. and will air on ESPN. It's official: Poch to Man United Sportscaster Dan Hicks dies Trenches Preview: Tennessee at Texas A&M COLUMBIA, SOUTH CAROLINA - NOVEMBER 07: T.J. Searcy #18 of the Texas A&M Aggies reacts in the second half against the South Carolina Gamecocks during their game at Williams-Brice Stadium on November 07, 2026 in Columbia, South Carolina. (Photo by Jacob Kupferman/Getty Images) | Getty Images Jay Arnold · SB Nation Wed, November 11, 2026 at 10:06 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Texas A&M returns to Kyle Field for the first time in three weeks after two straight road losses, sandwiched by an idle week. The Aggies fell 17-9 to South Carolina last time out in a contest that saw Texas A&M accumulate over 450 yards of offense and fail to produce a touchdown. The Aggies will hope to rectify that this week in College Station as they welcome the #8 Tennessee Volunteers to town. The trenches are going to be extremely important if Texas A&M is going to steal a win this Saturday. Let's dive into what needs to happen up front for the Aggies to come out on top. Offensive Line COLUMBIA, SOUTH CAROLINA - NOVEMBER 07: Marcel Reed #10 of the Texas A&M Aggies runs with the ball in the first half against the South Carolina Gamecocks during their game at Williams-Brice Stadium on November 07, 2026 in Columbia, South Carolina. (Photo by Jacob Kupferman/Getty Images) | Getty Images Against South Carolina, Texas A&M moved the ball well. As mentioned above, the Aggies racked up over 450 yards of offense. Rueben Owens ripped off multiple explosive runs, and Texas A&M had 206 yards on the ground. Yet, zero touchdowns made the hope that would be rendered by the yardage a grand disappointment instead. Simply put, field goals do not win games. The Aggies have to be able to finish drives off to win games, and Texas A&M has failed to do so in three out of the four road contests this season. The Texas A&M offense has fared better at home for the most part, but frankly I don't expect that to continue against an absolutely elite Tennessee defense. The Vols rank second only to Georgia in scoring defense. Tennessee's passing defense is staunch, though the Aggies wouldn't likely be able to test them there either. The rushing defense isn't in the upper tier of the conference but is also solid. Most significantly, the Volunteers lead the country in sacks. Defensive end Tyree Weathersby has seven sacks this season. The Vols also get pressure from the interior, as defensive tackle Xavier Gilliam has six sacks. Gilliam is a force to be reckoned with in the run game as well. I've thoroughly enjoyed watching film on the gifted DT this year, but I don't think his ability bodes well for this Texas A&M offensive line. I don't think this offensive line is horrible, and I think they've continued to play better as the season has progressed, but against this defensive front for Tennessee, it's going to feel like all that progress has left. In short, if the Aggies score a touchdown this week, I'd be surprised if it came from the offense. Defensive Line COLUMBIA, SOUTH CAROLINA - NOVEMBER 07: Marco Jones #10 of the Texas A&M Aggies plays against the South Carolina Gamecocks during their game at Williams-Brice Stadium on November 07, 2026 in Columbia, South Carolina. (Photo by Jacob Kupferman/Getty Images) | Getty Images While the situation for the offensive side of the ball is dire, I think the defensive side of the ball largely shouldered the burden well against South Carolina. The Aggies held what was the top rushing offense in the country at the time to under 100 yards right up until LaNorris Sellers ripped off a big run at the end. The Aggies also sacked Sellers twice, including a massive strip sack by Bryce Perry-Wright. We'll see if those run game improvements carry over as the Aggies face yet another powerful rushing attack. Powered by the legs of running back DeSean Bishop, Tennessee is the current top rushing attack in the SEC. However, if Texas A&M can find a way to slow down this rushing attack, the Aggies just might have a chance in this one. Discipline and sure tackling are going to be of the utmost importance as this Josh Heupel offense looks to spread opposing defenses out in order to capitalize on seams. Missed tackles against this Tennessee offense are extremely disastrous, and the Aggies can't afford to lose one-on-ones. The front four must maintain gap discipline as the secondary will be forced to honor Tennessee's formations. Get Tennessee behind the chains, and this becomes a drastically different ball game. While Tennessee ranks at the top of the conference in rushing, the Volunteers are the only team in the SEC below Texas A&M in passing offense. After Faizon Brandon started the season under center for Tennessee, George MacIntyre has since taken over. However, neither QB is a game changer on this offense, making the Vols basically one-dimensional. The equation for success against Tennessee is simple. Stop running backs DeSean Bishop and Daune Morris or get ground to a pulp. If the Aggies can make the improvements against the run permanent, they can hang around in this one – and that starts with the defensive tackle position and Brandon Davis-Swain, DJ Hicks, CJ Mims, and Landon Rink, in my opinion. While I think the Aggies keep this contest close in the first half, I think repeated three-and-outs by the Aggie offense eventually allow the Volunteers to wear down the Texas A&M defense in the second half. I have Tennessee winning this one 20-3. #BTHOtennessee

Published: Nov 12, 2026 · 10:00 AM EST The Tennessee Volunteers have come up with 2 of the most impressive wins of the season in the FBS, a 26-10 point pounding of Alabama and last weekend's 34-6 drubbing of Kentucky . Both teams were in the top 6 of the initial College Football Playoff Rankings. But despite the Vols being 7-2 with those 2 victories, and despite Tennessee's 2 losses each coming by a field goal against teams currently in the top 20 of those rankings, the Vols probably have to win out to make the field of 12. The Fearless Prediction knows how difficult it can be to win on the road in the SEC but will readily accept the challenge to make the correct call in Saturday's Tennessee- Texas A&M game. This will only be the second time that the Vols have made a trip to College Station. Back in 2016, they lost at Texas A&M in double overtime, 45-38, in a game best remembered for Tennessee RB Alvin Kamara's dominating performance. He had 18 carries for 127 yards and 2 TDs to go with 8 catches for 161 yards and a TD. It was the only game in Kamara's 2 seasons in Knoxville in which he was the focal point of the UT offense. If that doesn't summarize the missed opportunities of the Butch Jones era, nothing will. Fast forwarding to today, Tennessee's offense might not have a Kamara, but it does have a Bishop. The Vols' senior RB, DeSean Bishop, already has 1,066 rushing yards this season, and now stands 426 yards away from breaking Dylan Sampson's single-season rushing record of 1,491 rushing yards. Bishop (and Tennessee's offensive line) gets better as the game continues, and that certainly helps the cause with youth at QB. Redshirt freshman George MacIntyre completed 9-of-14 passes for 125 yards against UK, but more importantly he didn't throw an interception and he didn't fumble. But Josh Heupel added a wrinkle to the QB position, with true freshman Faizon Brandon (remember him?) seeing his first action since being pulled in the Auburn game a month ago. Brandon only took a couple of snaps. One in a single wing formation that resulted in a 29-yard run, and one a beautifully designed play in which Brandon tossed the football approximately 5 centimeters forward to Mike Matthews for what counts as a 24-yard TD pass. Heupel has now given opposing defensive coordinators more reason for concern the rest of the season, not knowing what else Heupel will come up with that Brandon package. Defensively, Tennessee continues to impress. It kept Kentucky out of the end zone for 60 minutes. It sacked UK QB Kenny Minchey 4 times while forcing 3 turnovers against a team that rarely coughed up the football. Tennessee is tied for 10th nationally in scoring defense (allowing 15.1 points per game), 18th in total defense (296.4 yards per game), and leads the nation in sacks with 39. LB Arion Carter is tops on the Vols in tackles with 59. DT Xavier Gilliam has a team-best 11.5 tackles for loss. As for Texas A&M, a season that began with so much promise has devolved into depression. The Aggies have lost 5 of their last 7 games, including a 17-9 defeat at South Carolina last weekend. They are 1-5 in SEC play. Mike Elko , now in his 3rd year as Texas A&M's head coach, has stuck with QB Marcel Reed, despite middling results. Reed throws for 182.3 yards per game, but his TD-to-INT ratio of 8:8 is not ideal. Rueben Owens II and K.J. Edwards combine to average 96.2 rushing yards per game. Mario Craver and Isaiah Horton are Reed's best options in the passing game, combining for 62 catches, 703 yards and 6 scores this season. Overall, the Aggies are only ranked 91st in the FBS in total offense, with 359.2 yards per game. The Aggies' defense will be a challenge for the Vols. ETSU and Tulsa transfer LB Ray Coney leads the team with 46 tackles. As a unit, they allow 320 yards per game, good enough to be ranked 28th nationally, while allowing only 18.7 points per game, 22nd in the FBS. Next week the Vols welcome Lane Kiffin and LSU back to Neyland Stadium. The Fearless Prediction will have a lot to say about that soon, but we aren't looking ahead. Tennessee better not either. And it won't. Kyle Field might be a tough place to play… but a lot of teams do win there. You'll be able to add Tennessee to that list. Fearless Prediction: Tennessee 24, Texas A&M 13 Mark Nagi has covered Tennessee athletics for over 20 years. He is the author of “Decade of Dysfunction,” an in-depth look at all that led to the crazy coaching search of 2017 at Tennessee. The book is available on Amazon. away.headline: Tennessee RB Daune Morris Suffers Leg Injury in Car Accident, Out Indefinitely
away.blurb: Camden Hall/Getty Images College Football The No. 8 Tennessee Volunteers will be without their second-leading rusher for some time. The school announced that running back Daune Morris suffered "non-life threatening injuries, including a broken leg" after a one-vehicle accident early Friday morning: A sophomore, Morris has rushed for 434 yards and three touchdowns on 66 carries this season, while also catching six passes for 35 yards. Morris played a significant role in the Vols' 34-6 drubbing of then-No. 6 Kentucky last weekend, rushing for 85 yards and a touchdown on just five carries. DeSean Bishop led the way on the ground for Tennessee, though, rushing for 109 yards and two scores. Bishop is the team's leading rusher this season with 1,066 yards and 13 touchdowns, and he figures to have an even bigger workload than usual on Saturday with Morris on the shelf. Meanwhile, Javin Gordon will likely operate as the RB2 after rushing for 129 yards and no touchdowns on 28 carries over five appearances this season. away.blurb: Morris has been the Vols’ most explosive option out of the backfield, rushing for 85 yards and a touchdown on just five carries in the win over Kentucky last weekend and going for a career-high 116 yards and a touchdown on 14 carries (8.3 yards per carry) in the Vols’ 42-9 win over Kennesaw State earlier in the year. Not having him in the rotation for the rest of the season is a significant blow for the team. Bishop will have to shoulder an even greater load, along with the help of sophomore backs Javin Gordon and Justin Baker. After Texas A&M on Saturday, Tennessee will host No. 21 LSU before closing out their regular season on the road at Vanderbilt. Tennessee is riding high after its 34-6 victory over Kentucky last weekend. The Volunteers improved to 7-2 overall and 4-2 in SEC play with the win, and moved to No. 8 in the latest College Football Playoff rankings, jumping up five spots from the week before. They’re in line to get back to the CFP, but will need a win Saturday at Texas A&M, with the Aggies sitting 4-5 overall and 1-5 in SEC in what’s been a disappointing year for Mike Elko’s squad. Unfortunately, the Vols will have to do it without one of their best offensive players, sophomore running back Daune Morris. Morris was involved in an overnight car accident on Thursday, sustaining a leg injury, and is now set to miss the remainder of the 2026 season, according to CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz. More news : NFL Draft Expert Makes Bold Claim About Oklahoma State QB Drew Mestemaker It’s an absolute momentum killer for Tennessee. The Vols are one of the most run-heavy teams in college football , leading the SEC with 216 rushing yards per game, of which Morris is responsible for a large chunk. He has 434 rushing yards and three rushing touchdowns on 66 carries in nine games this season, averaging 6.6 yards per carry. Morris is the top running back behind starter DeSean Bishop, an All-SEC back who already has 1,066 rushing yards and 13 rushing touchdowns on the year, both of which rank second in the conference, averaging 5.4 yards per carry. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings The reigning national champion and ninth-ranked Hoosiers look to avoid a potentially devastating second loss when they host No. 18 USC Getty Images No. 9 Indiana is feeling the heat for its Big Ten showdown with No. 18 USC on Saturday after falling five spots in the College Football Playoff rankings during its bye week. But the Hoosiers, who have yet to announce a starting quarterback for the game, can calm the waters by notching a quality win over the visiting Trojans. USC is lagging outside the CFP picture…for now. That will change if the Trojans can upset IU on the road after beating Ohio State in their last game during Week 9. A win would also catapult USC into the Big Ten title race, revitalizing a season that appeared to be in peril after a 24-7 loss at Wisconsin on Oct. 24. The question is which Indiana quarterback the Trojans will be tasked with defending. Season-long starter Josh Hoover injured his throwing arm during Indiana's Week 9 win over Minnesota and was benched after subsequent struggles. Veteran backup Grant Wilson entered and completed 9 of 17 passes for 156 yards and a touchdown, sparking a quarterback controversy. Hoosiers coach Curt Cignetti was noncommittal this week on who will take the first snaps for IU, forcing USC to be ready for either option. The situation has created some late-season intrigue for the reigning national champions, who have been unable to pull away from most of their Big Ten opponents during an 8-1 (5-1 Big Ten) start. USC vs. Indiana: Need to know Can USC match Indiana's physicality?: Regardless of who is at quarterback for Indiana, USC's defense will have its hands full with the Hoosiers' skill talent. Physical receivers Charlie Becker and Nick Marsh comprise one of the best 1-2 tandems in college football. Meanwhile, IU running backs Turbo Richard and Lee Beebe Jr . are both averaging more than five yards per carry and are over 700 yards each for the season. USC has never been known for its physicality under coach Lincoln Riley, but keeping the Hoosiers in check will require it. Going on the road and winning against a team with Indiana's gritty DNA wouldn't just be a huge boost for the Trojans' playoff aspirations; it would also help change the perception of Riley's program. Indiana's CFP outlook: Indiana's chances of making the playoff will reach near "lock" status at 96.2% with a win, according to the CBS Sports CFP Forecaster. A loss would leave the Hoosiers with a 66.8% chance of selection and bring greater scrutiny to a resume lacking high-end fare. An Oct. 10 win over Nebraska is not aging well, as the Cornhuskers are on a four-game losing streak. After that, IU's best win is either on the road against a 5-4 Michigan team or at home against a 6-3 Northwestern team. However you slice it, the Hoosiers don't have a win against a team currently ranked in the CFP Top 25. Beating USC would change that...assuming the Trojans remain in the rankings. USC's CFP outlook: This is do-or-die for USC's playoff hopes. The Trojans' chances of making the field will rise to 51.5% with a win and plummet to 3.7% with a loss. In other words, the playoff has already started for Lincoln Riley's team. It's really a simple formula: finish 3-0 with wins over Indiana, Maryland and USC, and the Trojans will unquestionably make the playoff for the first time. Lose any of those games, and it's probably over for what is arguably the most historic program to have never appeared in the CFP. Where to watch USC vs. Indiana live Date : Saturday, Nov. 14 | Time : 3:30 p.m. ET Location : Memorial Stadium -- Bloomington, Indiana TV: CBS | Live stream: CBSSports.com , CBS Sports App Streaming on Paramount+ Premium USC vs. Indiana prediction, picks Five of Indiana's six Big Ten games have been decided by a touchdown or less. The only exception was a 47-15 win against an overmatched Rutgers team. The Hoosiers haven't shown the ability to pull away and dominate quality opposition. So long as IU limits catastrophic turnovers, it will win the game on the basis of its physicality on both lines of scrimmage. But it's difficult to envision the Hoosiers suddenly pulling away from a team of USC's caliber. The Trojans have a veteran quarterback in Jayden Maiava who can keep his team in the game. The Trojans have a legitimate chance to shake up the Big Ten race, give their College Football Playoff resume another major boost and send a strong message about the direction of their program. The Trojans are gearing up for a season-altering matchup against the No. 9 Indiana Hoosiers on the road in Bloomington. Indiana currently ranks fifth nationally in total defense, allowing just 259.2 yards per game. However, that number doesn't tell the whole story when it comes to the Hoosiers' ability to defend high-volume passing attacks. USC is averaging 294.5 passing yards per game while completing 67.3 percent of its attempts. USC quarterback Jayden Maiava has been a major reason for that success, throwing for 2,525 yards and 20 touchdowns while completing 67.3 percent of his passes. The Trojans also have no shortage of weapons for Maiava to work with. Freshman wide receiver Trent Mosley leads USC's receiving corps with 32 catches for 512 yards and six touchdowns, while fellow freshman Kayden Dixon-Wyatt has recorded 32 receptions for 443 yards and four touchdowns. Pete Fiutak · College Football News Thu, November 12, 2026 at 4:37 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Just when it seemed like USC was finished, and a new era would soon start with Lincoln Riley all but gone after an ugly 24-7 loss at Wisconsin, a funny thing happened – the Trojans rolled Ohio State 30-18. And now, at 7-2, with high-profile dates remaining against CFP No. 9 Indiana and No. 8 UCLA, No. 18 USC all but controls its own path to the CFP – a 10-2 Trojan team with two top-ten wins in the final three games wouldn't be a lock to get in, but … yeah, it would be. But Indiana is still pretty good. It's 8-1, this close to being 9-0, and even though the schedule hasn't been a killer, if it keeps winning, all will be just fine. But lose this, and the pressure will be on to avoid a slip over the last two weeks. USC vs Indiana: Quick Hits Indiana travels to Washington after this before finishing with the rivalry date against Purdue. USC hosts Maryland after this before the showdown at UCLA. It's just the fifth meeting ever, and the first since USC joined the Big Ten. The Trojans are 4-0, including the 1968 Rose Bowl. How To Watch USC vs Indiana Date: Saturday, November 14, 2026 Game Time: 3:30 PM ET TV: CBS Location: Memorial Stadium, Bloomington, IN – Week 11 Schedule, Predictions – CFN Bowl & CFP Projections | Top 25 – How many 3-loss CFP teams will there be? Why USC Will Win Plenty of things have to go right. USC has the punting to own the field position game, there can't be a slew of turnovers, and Indiana has to keep struggling. The only way to put it is that it's like the Hoosiers forgot how to score. The offense is moving a bit, but it hasn't scored more than 20 points in regulation since early October. The USC passing game continues to be good enough. The ground game might be hit-or-miss, but Jayden Maiava is a smart, tough veteran who keeps hitting his throws for the Big Ten's best offense on third downs. Why Indiana Will Win Indiana got a week off to reset at just the right time. No, it's not playing nearly as well offensively as it did last year. No, it doesn't have that dominant mode, and it certainly doesn't have the same passing game. And yet it's still 8-1 – this bunch finds ways to win. For all of the issues on offense, the defense continues to be outstanding. The run D is the fourth-best in the nation, allowing just 2.3 yards per carry overall with no touchdowns in the last three games. USC might throw well, but it wasn't all that long ago that the ground game was stuffed for -18 yards by Wisconsin. USC vs Indiana Prediction, Betting Lines Is Grant Wilson up to the gig, or will Josh Hoover get the nod as he fights through an injury? No matter who ends up under center, he'll be fine against a USC defense that's been hit hard by injuries. Indiana's offense – even without banged up star RB Turbo Richard – will be a bit more effective than it was against Ohio State, Michigan, or Minnesota, but it'll be the defensive front and run defense that keeps the good season going. Brian Kelly, now a commentator for CBS Sports, knows what it's like to coach in the state of Indiana. He recently said on air that Lincoln Riley's Trojans will go into Bloomington and win. Brian Kelly has no real reason to pick games for any reason other than he sincerely thinks one team will beat the other, but it's notable that he would trust USC and distrust Indiana. Both schools' fan bases don't like Notre Dame. It is simply interesting to wonder why Kelly is pivoting to the Trojans and away from the Hoosiers. Is there any underlying emotional reality which might have nudged Kelly in the direction of USC? Let's keep in mind that Kelly wants to return to coaching. Is his USC pick in any way motivated by how he sees the coaching carousel or the national landscape? We'll never know the answers, but the questions are legitimately interesting. away.blurb: The No. 9 Hoosiers (8-1, 5-1 Big Ten) do have some other injury concerns going into a must-win game against the No. 18 Trojans (7-2, 4-2). They four key contributors (three starters) on the report with leading rusher Turbo Richard and defensive end Kellan Wyatt already listed as out for Saturday's game. Indiana has been down at least one running back — Khobie Martin missed half the season with an arm injury — for much of the year. Martin made his return to the lineup against the Gophers, but he only has three carries for seven yards on the season. The Hoosiers also listed cornerback A.J. Harris and linebacker Rolijah Hardy as questionable. Hardy was a late scratch against Minnesota with a back injury while Harris hobbled off the field in the second half. Harris missed time earlier this season with a knee injury, but played well after regaining his spot in the starting lineup. Jaylen Bell, who stepped in for Harris earlier this season, would likely get the start if the Penn State transfer is ruled out. picks.blurb: Michigan at No. 16 Oregon College Football Preview - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Commanders edge Giants Skattebo's spooky stare 'Who Let the Dogs Out'? It's official: Poch to Man United Sportscaster Dan Hicks dies Michigan at No. 16 Oregon College Football Preview Kyle Yost · SB Nation Fri, November 13, 2026 at 3:00 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Everything is bad! Maybe a (long overdue) change at offensive coordinator will help a little, but the dead cat bounce at quarterback lasted exactly two quarters. Now even that switch seems up in the air, as the Michigan Wolverines try to somehow get to bowl eligibility, which actually is far from guaranteed with three tough games remaining. First among those is a date with the Oregon Ducks, who shockingly already have three losses — and a lost quarterback — yet are somehow back in the playoff hunt. Like Kyle Whittingham, Dan Lanning has also made a change at coordinator, and back-to-back ranked wins have the Ducks well positioned for a 9-3 finish with a real shot at the CFP, and even the (final!) Big Ten Championship Game. Vibes are pretty lopsided heading into Saturday, and this would not be the first time Michigan has faced Oregon after a humiliating defeat. That 2007 contest did not go super well, and the 2026 edition is likely to repeat history, but at this point who knows anything. Frustration has turned to apathy in Ann Arbor, so this weekend really only has upside…right? Michigan (5-4, 2-4) at No. 16 Oregon (6-3, 4-2) Date & Time : Saturday, Nov. 14, 3:30 p.m. ET Location : Autzen Stadium, Eugene, OR TV/Streaming : FS1 These teams have met once already as conference foes, with the then-No. 1 Ducks earning the win at the Big House over a 5-3 Michigan team that looked pretty rough under Sherrone Moore and Wink Martindale. Davis Warren only threw for 165 yards that game but posted 7.2 YPA and two touchdowns. At best, this program is no better off than it was 24 months ago, and arguably is in worse shape now. Offense: Deck chairs Week after week this offense finds new ways to disappoint, but last Saturday really felt like rock bottom. There were no redeeming qualities from the debacle against State, aside from finally breaking the camel's back, and while the removal of Jason Beck likely helps, how much it will actually improve the No. 126-ranked scoring offense is up for debate. The Ducks are middle of the pack in points per game and yards per game, and are equally effective against the run and pass. Losing edge Teitum Tuioti is a tough blow, but this defense should still be ok against Michigan without him. Objectively, Oregon's defense has taken a step back this season, but it might be hitting its stride at the right time. If the Wolverines struggle to move the ball, it is quite possible Bryce Underwood gets some snaps. To the surprise of no one, the lights have been too bright for Tommy Carr, and the downside of Underwood is no worse than his successor's. The lingering reason for hope is the run game, as Jordan Marshall and Savion Hiter are far too good to be putting up such awful numbers. Beck is gone, and hopefully is the rhino; better play calling is a must. Defense: Do your job Whittingham's only pathway for the rest of the season is turning every game into the 2024 Ohio State win that sees the defense do enough to pull off the low-scoring upset. Even with some annoying moments last weekend, this unit is capable of doing just that. The pressure is immense knowing how much burden it must carry for the offense, but SP+ still considers this a top-three defense. Oregon replaced an injured Dante Moore with Dylan Raiola, who has been pretty solid thus far with 11 touchdowns to just two interceptions and a 65-percent completion rate on 7.3 YPA. He lit up Northwestern and did well against Ohio State, getting the ball to stud receiver Dakorien Moore. The Ducks are definitely a tricky offense to go against, especially when they feel confident in the passing game. However, the run game has been much less impressive, in part due to a bad offensive line. Jay Hill will have a chance to overwhelm up front and make Raiola uncomfortable, trusting the secondary to lock up receivers long enough to stall out drives. One thing to watch is fumbles, as Oregon has the second-most losses (10) in the country this season, though that is skewed by the bizarre afternoon against UCLA. Michigan needs one more win. Before the season started, this weekend was arguably the most obvious loss, then Oregon started looking bad and there was a glimmer of optimism, but since then the teams have gone in opposite directions. With red-hot UCLA up next, is the best chance for victory somehow in Columbus? What even is this season. I do not expect the Wolverines to win on Saturday, even with Beck gone and Underwood potentially back in. That is unfortunate, as this Oregon team is seemingly as vulnerable as it ever will be, and the Michigan defense has a chance to play fairly evenly on that side of the ball. The same cannot be said for the ground attack, though, which will not take advantage of the Ducks' front seven like Oklahoma State and Northwestern did. That leaves us in a weird place where I do not think a blowout is the most likely outcome, but neither is an upset. Oregon has done enough to save its season, while Whittingham has essentially done the opposite, more likely to lose his job after every week. Even a minor resurgence on offense could be enough for a favorable result, but that would be a pretty big surprise.

picks.headline: Ducks Wire staff predicts Oregon Ducks vs. Michigan Wolverines
picks.blurb: None of that is possible if they don't win the remainder of games on their schedule, though, and they face one of the best defenses on their schedule this week with the Michigan Wolverines coming to town. While Michigan's offense has been putrid over the last few weeks, they have a change at offensive coordinator and have yet to allow more than 21 points in a single game this year. However, the Ducks' offense has been clicking as of late, and there should be some real optimism that they can find success once again, this time at home in front of an excited Autzen crowd. So, what does Saturday have in store? That's a tough question to answer. To preview the game, we go through our weekly roundtable with the writers from Ducks Wire to offer our opinions and predictions for what's to come. Here is our roundtable conversation. Ohio State Rewind Question: Well, I don't think many people saw THAT coming. Oregon went into the Horseshoe, fell behind 14-0, and proceeded to score 38 unanswered points in a 41-28 win over Ohio State. What was the most impressive part of that performance, and has it changed your outlook on what this team can accomplish this season? Zachary Neel: I think it was the way in which we saw the offense operate. It wasn't a persistent ground attack, or chunk play after chunk play through the air, but instead a heavy dose of the intermediate passing game, picking up 10-15 yards at a time through the air. The Ducks were very good on 3rd and long, which was good to see, and the offense in general seemed to flow much better than we've seen all year. Don Smalley: Let's face it, earlier in the year, down 14-0 on the road at Ohio State, that game would have been over. But instead of giving up, the Ducks came together and ran off one of the most impressive offensive performances I've seen in a long time. Teams, even the great teams, don't go into the horseshoe and score 38 straight points. Oregon's resiliency was the most impressive thing in that game. A successful fake punt didn't hurt either. If that didn't work, Lanning would have been called a complete moron, and a lot more people would be calling for his job. Thankfully, it worked. Fired up the team, and now Lanning is a genius. Bjorn Bergstrom: For the second straight week, it was not having any quit after falling behind by two scores early. Last week, the Ducks didn’t fold in that spot, an anomaly from the first two months of the season. But they proved that their mental and physical resiliency is becoming a trend and something that Oregon can rely on when things get tough. Logan Brown: I was really impressed by the offensive line’s performance, not only keeping Dylan Raiola clean, but executing in the run game in the second half. The Ducks had a ton of push and were able to get linemen out in space to block downfield as well. That is a far cry from where the unit was earlier in the season, and if the Ducks can continue to run the ball down the stretch, they can certainly go on a run. Offensive Turnaround Question: Just a few weeks ago, Oregon's offense looked completely lost, and Drew Mehringer was fired as offensive coordinator. Now, with Jay Johnson calling plays and Dylan Raiola under center, the Ducks have scored 75 points over their last two games. How much of this turnaround do you attribute to Johnson, how much to Raiola, and how confident are you that it will continue? Zachary Neel: I give a little bit more of the credit to Johnson than I do Raiola, because we still have seen a number of balls put into jeopardy from No. 8, but he's been lucky with the defense failing to capitalize. More importantly, though, I give a lot of the credit to the offensive line, which has played incredibly well over the last two games, not giving up a single sack since the loss to Illinois. Don Smalley: I think it's 50/50. Raiola has been very good, but the offensive line has been great. They've protected him, let him throw downfield. That touchdown to Dakorian Moore was a prominent example of that. Bjorn Bergstrom: A lot of it’s Johnson, who’s taken the reins and clearly instilled confidence in his players to go out and make plays. While he’s a part of putting the players in position to make plays, Raiola is the connector, and he’s doing an awfully good job of hearing what the objective of the play is and doing his part so the skill players can do their job as well. I would say that we’ll find out if it can continue once we hit some rough patches, but the first quarter of each game was a rough patch, and the Ducks offense emerged. So, I’m pretty confident this is real. Logan Brown: Jay Johnson was pretty masterful against Ohio State. There were countless times when he set up the defense with a certain look and came back to it later with a wrinkle that led to a big play. He correctly diagnosed Ohio State’s heavy blitzes on third down and used the screen game to his advantage. It’s little things like that which will take the Ducks where they want to go. Raiola has played better, but some of his decisions under pressure and his footwork are very concerning. He should continue to play at a high level, but I do fear his flirting with trouble will eventually catch up to him. A Dominant Defense Question: Let's show the defense some love. After giving up 14 points in the first quarter, Oregon completely shut down Ohio State for the next two quarters, allowing just 39 total yards. Who or what deserves the most credit for that defensive turnaround, and what does it tell you about this unit going forward? Zachary Neel: Chris Hampton is starting to get the flowers that he deserves, but I want to shout out the linebackers on this team. There were some questions about that unit going into the year, and so far, they have improved greatly from Week 1 and turned into one of the best positions on the defense. The cornerbacks have also been very good, and they did a superb job of stopping Jeremiah Smith this past weekend. Don Smalley: I don't think Chris Hampton is getting as much praise as he deserves. The defense has improved a lot this year. They are aggressive when they need to be and fall back when the time comes. Bjorn Bergstrom: For the first time in two seasons, the Ducks’ front seven finally seems to be getting consistent pressure on the quarterback. Last season, the secondary was so good that blitzes weren’t really needed. But with the secondary struggling a bit in 2026, Chris Hampton had to turn up the pressure notch a bit, and it worked out tremendously. The Ducks were flying around in Columbus, turning up the heat on Luke Fahey and making him see ghosts. This unit, like the offense, is for real. Logan Brown: I don’t think any one coach or player deserves more credit than the other. I think the Ducks have just come together and played well off each other. The pass rush has taken care of business, and the secondary has done enough to hold down explosive passing attacks in recent weeks. Oregon isn’t hurting itself with many missed tackles, and while there is still a weakness or two that teams can expose, the Ducks have been timely with their calls on critical downs. They will miss Teitum Tuioti moving forward, but I think the defensive prowess is sustainable. Question: Oregon's win over Ohio State has breathed new life into its postseason aspirations. The Ducks still need help elsewhere, but the possibility of reaching the Big Ten Championship Game and potentially the College Football Playoff is back on the table. How optimistic are you about Oregon's chances of making a run, and what’s the likelihood, in your mind, that they can potentially grab an at-large bid? Zachary Neel: I'd say it's about 33/33/33 right now that Oregon gets in as an at-large, gets into the Big Ten title game, or misses the playoff altogether. A ton is going to play out over the next couple of weeks, so it will be fascinating to watch, but ultimately, I'm just thankful that we're still having this conversation. It's good for business. Don Smalley: With the Ohio State game out of the way, unless the wheels come completely off, the Ducks should be able to run the table. They'll be favored big over Michigan, Michigan State, and Washington. In order to make the playoff, Oregon might have to get the Big Ten Championship Game and of course, win it. I like their chances. Bjorn Bergstrom: I’m very optimistic. Of course, the Ducks have to win their final three regular season games and look good doing so, but if they do and chaos ensues — as it has for much of the season — above them, an at-large bid is within the realm of possibility. Obviously, making the Big Ten title game and beating what’s likely to be UCLA is the most likely scenario, in my opinion, but the way Oregon has looked, they deserve to be evaluated for an at-large spot. Logan Brown: So far with the rankings, the selection committee seems to be fans of Oregon, making them the highest-ranked three-loss team. I still think Oregon’s best shot to make the field is to win the Big Ten, but there is a path without making it to the game, though that involves a lot of chaos in front of them and some style points the rest of the way. I think the Ducks have a 35% chance of making it to the playoffs right now, which feels crazy to say given where the program was a few weeks ago. Michigan Wolverines Question: Michigan comes to Autzen Stadium this weekend, and Oregon is suddenly playing some of its best football of the season. After such an emotional win in Columbus, what concerns you most about this matchup with the Wolverines? What's the biggest key to avoiding a letdown and keeping the momentum rolling? Zachary Neel: There are two things that worry me: Michigan's defense and Oregon's inconsistency this year. They are trending in the right direction and have been playing great football for the last six quarters, but I am still very aware that we could see some bad football at any moment in time. The Wolverines' defense has the ability to pull mistakes out of you, so I'm very aware of that. Don Smalley: There has been a history of teams suffering a letdown a week after a big win. I think with the game being at home and Michigan playing a true freshman, the odds are in the Ducks' favor. I would be surprised if Oregon suffers a letdown of any kind this week. Bjorn Bergstrom: I’m worried about the Wolverines pulling the Ducks underwater and forcing them to play their brand of football, which is low-scoring and defense-oriented. That’s the type of ball we saw from Oregon in their worst three-game stretch of the year against UCLA, Nebraska, and Illinois, and I’m afraid that the Ducks wouldn’t do well in that again. Oregon has to continue to play free and not tentative against a very good defense. They need to dictate the style of football that’s played. Logan Brown: The conditions may not be ideal on Saturday, but Oregon still needs to find a way to start fast for once. It hasn’t happened despite the recent success, and the Ducks have needed to claw back from down multiple scores to win. If the Ducks can score a touchdown or two in the first quarter, that might be enough to win the game. The longer this game remains a one-possession difference, the better it serves Michigan and their ferocious defense. Gambling Corner Question: Gambling Corner: You get $100 to spread across the point spread (Oregon -10.5), and the Over/Under (36.5 points). How are you allocating your funds? Zachary Neel: I like to think Oregon can win this game by double digits, but I'm not positive. I am very confident, however, that this will be a low-scoring game. Give me $100 on the under. Don Smalley: I would put $80 on Oregon covering the spread and the rest on the over. Bjorn Bergstrom: This is a really tough one. Nobody’s been able to score on Michigan’s defense, and they haven’t even been able to score themselves. So I’ll go all $100 on the under, though I think the Ducks have a good shot at covering. It's official: Poch to Man United Sportscaster Dan Hicks dies Sam Hutchens, Mississippi Clarion Ledger · The Clarion Ledger Thu, November 12, 2026 at 11:03 AM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads OXFORD − Ole Miss football must win on the road against Oklahoma to keep hopes of a College Football Playoff appearance alive. No. 17 Ole Miss (6-3, 4-3 SEC) will play at Oklahoma (5-4, 3-3) on Nov. 14 (3:15 p.m., SEC Network). The Rebels are coming off a 42-7 home loss to No. 1 Georgia that put its CFP hopes on the edge of extinction. A viable path to the CFP begins with winning the final three games of the season. This is the third consecutive season Ole Miss has faced Oklahoma and the Rebels have won the first two matchups. Like Ole Miss, the Sooners made the College Football Playoff in 2025. OU returned quarterback John Mateer but has struggled to complement a strong defense with a steady offense. Although the Sooners have losses to Michigan, No. 1 Georgia, No. 13 Kentucky and No. 24 South Carolina, OU has beaten two teams that Ole Miss lost to in No. 8 Texas and Florida. Here are five predictions about the matchup, including the final score: Jason Witten will have new wrinkles for OU offense vs Ole Miss defense The matchup pits defensive coaches against each other in Ole Miss' Pete Golding and OU's Brent Venables. Interim offensive coordinator Jason Witten could be the wild card. The former Dallas Cowboys tight end was elevated to the interim offensive coordinator position after Oklahoma fired Ben Arbuckle. Five days after Arbuckle was dismissed, OU beat Florida 23-7 in a game where it had 351 total yards. The Oklahoma offense played clean, efficient football under Witten. The Sooners suddenly seem to have new life offensively, which comes at a bad time for an Ole Miss defense that was ravaged for 481 yards vs Georgia. Trinidad Chambliss, John Mateer both throw interceptions With three games remaining, Chambliss' interceptions have tripled this season. He threw three in a spectacular 2025 season, but is up to nine in 2026. Golding attributed the increase to a combination of bad reads, bad luck and bad throws. Chambliss has thrown at least one interception in seven games this season. That plays into the hands of Oklahoma, which is No. 4 in the SEC with nine interceptions. The Sooners are also No. 5 in the conference with 26 sacks. Chambliss has been more vulnerable when under pressure. OU quarterback John Mateer has had turnover problems as well. He's thrown seven interceptions and has two lost fumbles. Look for both defenses to come up with an interception. The Sooners' stingy defense is better prepared to recover from interceptions than Ole Miss. When OU picks off Chambliss, it will give the ball back to a Sooners' offense that looks well prepared to chew clock and limit the chances for the Rebels' offense. Ole Miss gives Makhi Frazier, Shekai Mills-Knight both at least 10 carries Even with a quarterback as capable as Chambliss, it will be hard for Ole Miss to attack Oklahoma through the air. OU has the No. 1 passing defense in the SEC (170.7 yards per game). OU is No. 7 in the SEC in rushing defense (122.6 yards per game), but it's the weaker of two stout options. Ole Miss needs running backs Shekai Mills-Knight and Makhi Frazier to play well. Those two players are the primary backs with Kewan Lacy ruled out with a shoulder injury. Mills-Knight and Frazier combined for 17 carries for 60 yards vs Georgia, but they should get more carries against Oklahoma. Oklahoma leads in time of possession, Ole Miss relies on big plays Opponents are 31-for-112 (27.7%) on third down conversions against the Sooners. That's the lowest mark in the SEC and No. 4 nationally. That indicates Ole Miss will have trouble maintaining long, slow-developing drives. The key to combat that is explosive plays. Ole Miss could use a big game from Deuce Alexander. The receiver leads Ole Miss with 669 receiving yards, but he was held without a catch against Georgia. He is Ole Miss' fastest, most explosive player and the primary threat to score a deep touchdown. Ole Miss is on the other end of the spectrum. The Rebels allow 44% of third down conversions, which is No. 14 in the SEC. The Sooners clinched the game against Florida with a 20-play march in the fourth quarter that consumed 12:45 on the clock. The Rebels must avoid that fate. Ole Miss vs Oklahoma score prediction Oklahoma 24, Ole Miss 23: This should be a close game that will be determined by whether Ole Miss' defense or Oklahoma's offense does better. Right now it feels like the OU offense has more momentum. The Rebels are more desperate, but feeling like you need to press and make big plays on the road against OU's defense is a bad place to be. picks.blurb: Ole Miss vs. Oklahoma Predictions: Rebel Walk Staff Picks and Bold Calls - The Rebel Walk About Us About Us Meet the RW Team Advertising Information Football Featured Around the SEC: November 14 Football Schedule, Kickoff Times, TV and Radio Info Column | Before we know it, Trinidad Chambliss’ Saturdays at Ole Miss will be memories Recent Ole Miss vs. Oklahoma Predictions: Rebel Walk Staff Picks, X-Factors and Bold Calls THURSDAY Ole Miss vs. Oklahoma Injury Report: Frazier Now Questionable; Chambliss, Alexander No Longer Listed How to Watch Ole Miss vs. Oklahoma: Kickoff Time, TV, Radio, Odds and Weather On Air with Evie Basketball Featured Ole Miss Routs Southeastern Louisiana for Third Straight 90-Point Game to Open Season Patton Pinkins Scores 19 as Ole Miss Beats Central Arkansas 92-60 Recent TRANSCRIPT: Everything Chris Beard Said After Ole Miss' 99-58 Win Over Alcorn State Ole Miss Men's Basketball Rolls Past Alcorn State 99-58 in Season Opener Beyond the Bloodlines: 5-Star PG Tai Bell Calls Ole Miss' Beard 'One of the Best Coaches' Men's Articles Women's Articles Baseball Featured Ole Miss Baseball Lands 2028 No. 2 Recruit Tyce Johnson Ole Miss Baseball Releases 2027 Schedule: Maryland Opens Season, Oklahoma Visits Oxford Recent ‘I've got to go out there and earn it’: Hunter Elliott returns with something to prove as Ole Miss opens fall TRANSCRIPT: Mike Bianco talks newcomers, leadership and early standouts ahead of Ole Miss' Samford matchup When the cheering stops, the Ole Miss family remains: Rebel Hope Alliance offers a lifeline to former athletes More Sports Hockey Posted by Parks Burcham | Nov 12, 2026 | Football , Ole Miss Norman, Okla. – After a devastating 42-7 loss inside Vaught-Hemingway Stadium to the Georgia Bulldogs, the Ole Miss Rebels now travel to face the Oklahoma Sooners. This game should be a true test of whether Pete Golding has a group with the gumption to rebound after such a tough loss. Our staff offers thoughts on the matchup in Norman. Staff Predictions Parks Burcham Score Prediction: Ole Miss 27, Oklahoma 21 I don't think this game will be the prettiest in the world, but I do think Ole Miss will pick itself up off the floor and bounce back with a win. It will be a tight one. The Rebels haven't fared well on the road this season, but if they can stop Oklahoma's offensive momentum and the offense rekindles, they can get the job done. X-Factor: Trinidad Chambliss Chambliss is my X-Factor because he will be coming off another tough game for him this season. He cannot let what rattled him last week take over. He has to stay level-headed, come out confident, and put the cape back on because his team needs him to have a great day on the gridiron. Bold Prediction: Ole Miss defense slows down Oklahoma on the run Score Prediction: Ole Miss 24, Oklahoma 17 X Factor Player: Luke Ferrelli With Keaton Thomas out, Luke Ferrelli is going to need to play an expanded role against a really good rushing offense. I think it comes down to the Rebels' ability to stop the run and Ferrelli taking a majority of the green dot this weekend. Bold Prediction: Ole Miss wins the turnover battle John Mateer has struggled to take care of the ball this year, and I believe Ole Miss will take advantage of that this weekend to give them the edge. Luke Dunavant Score Prediction: Ole Miss 17, Oklahoma 20 Cue Loser by Tame Impala. With it now being official (even though we already knew it) that Kewan Lacy is out for the remainder of the season, the Texas Longhorns' bipolarization of this offense gives me cause for concern. X-Factor: Does this Team still want to Play Football? With their season almost effectively done, how does this team respond to that type of conclusion? Bold prediction: Caleb Cunningham plays A LOT I have this running bit with Billy and Parks. It seems as if Caleb Cunningham plays every other game, and this is an other game, so he is due to go off again. Jacob Quaglino Score Prediction: Ole Miss 27, Oklahoma 24 X Factor Player: Trinidad Chambliss A theme this season, so far, seems to be that the entire team plays as well as its QB plays. On days when Chambliss is off a bit, the team as a whole typically doesn't play well, seemingly indicating that Chambliss may well be the X factor player in just about every game moving forward. Playing on the road has been a struggle for this team as a whole. Oklahoma brings in one of the best pass defenses in the SEC, illustrating the importance of the Grand Rapids, MI native's performance on Saturday and his ability to play to the potential that we know he can play to. A single game—in reference to last week—does not ever have to define a player's season, or that of his team. Bold Prediction: Chambliss is both the team's leading passer and rusher for the game Well, perhaps not all that “bold,” but with Lacy now out for the rest of the season, the pressure ramps up on the rest of the team—not just the rest of the running backs—to pick up the slack. Chambliss has shown time and again his versatility with his legs, an ability that may well be crucial in a hostile road environment. And in a game like this, with a narrow road to the CFP barely alive, and needing to win out and get help to get there, Chambliss is going to have to show everyone why he was considered one of the best QB's in the nation during the preseason. The room for error is gone, and all options available to Golding's team may need to be used from here on out. Score Prediction: Ole Miss 24, Oklahoma 21 Ole Miss looks to bounce back after a 42-7 loss to then-No. 2 Georgia at home last Saturday. This week the Rebels will travel to Norman. Trinidad Chambliss throws for 200 yards with two touchdowns through the air and one with his legs. Bold Prediction: The Rebels' defense will stop Oklahoma's run to come away with a close victory in the end. Score Prediction: Ole Miss 31, Oklahoma 17 I think the Rebels will respond this week after getting dominated by Georgia; the lines on both sides of the ball will come out with something to prove after their physicality was tested last week. The defense has an opportunity to have a solid game against an Oklahoma offense that has struggled all year. X-Factor: Deuce Alexander My X-Factor this week is Deuce Alexander; he sustained a slight injury last Saturday but is expected to play against the Sooners, and he'll need a big game to open up Trinidad Chambliss' passing game against an extremely solid Oklahoma defense. Bold Prediction: Rebel Defense has one of its best games I think the defense will have one of their best games of the year against Oklahoma. They looked to be completely outmatched against the run game of Georgia, but with Oklahoma's struggles to run the ball, this would be a great time for the land shark defense to show up and help the squad keep some hope for the season alive. Score Prediction: Ole Miss 17, Oklahoma 21 Ole Miss returns to the field this Saturday following one of the most discouraging losses in recent memory. They'll travel to Oklahoma to face a Sooners team that's been extremely hot and cold. I believe the Sooners' defense will be too much for Ole Miss to handle and that Oklahoma will win this game 21-17. My X-Factor: Shekai Mills-Knight My X-Factor will come down to pass protection and the impact of Shekai Mills-Knight in the run game. Bold Prediction: Oklahoma records over 1.5 sacks on Trinidad Chambliss. Evie Van Pelt Score prediction: Ole Miss 31, Oklahoma 20 Oklahoma's defense is the best in the SEC against the pass, but the Sooners also have the league's lowest-ranked rushing offense. The Rebels score 33.8 points a game, and I expect them to land a little under that in Norman. Oklahoma scores 22.1 points a game, which is about what I'd give the Sooners. The Rebels' offense is more reliable on third down (48.8% to Oklahoma's 39.1%) and in the red zone (31 of 33 scoring). That gap decides a game that's close for three quarters. X-factor: RB Shekai Mills-Knight With Kewan Lacy out, now for the season, the Rebels need a back to take pressure off Trinidad Chambliss, because Oklahoma's pass defense could be more difficult to move against through the air. Mills-Knight has 33 carries for 165 yards and three touchdowns this season, so he has been used sparingly but has found the end zone. Makhi Frazier has had most of the carries (72 for 365 yards), but he is also on the injury report as of Thursday night. So Mills-Knight's role could be critical. If Ole Miss gets him enough touches, especially near the goal line, the offense stays balanced and doesn't rely on Chambliss throwing into the SEC's top pass defense. If he doesn't get them, the Rebels will have to win through the air. Bold predictions: Chambliss accounts for three touchdowns, one of them rushing, and Ole Miss holds Oklahoma under 100 rushing yards Oklahoma has the SEC's best pass defense, so Trinidad Chambliss might need his legs near the goal line. He already has 25 total touchdowns, seven of them rushing, and Ole Miss has scored on 31 of 33 red zone trips. The Rebels also have a clear edge against Oklahoma's rushing offense, which averages 110.9 yards and 3.23 yards a carry, the lowest in the SEC. Georgia and Florida each ran for about 300 yards on this defense, but Ole Miss held Auburn to 63 on Oct. 31st. Oklahoma is more likely to look like the Auburn game than the Georgia game in that respect. Score Prediction: Ole Miss 23, Oklahoma 21 Other than hammering Vanderbilt in Nashville, the Rebels haven't had much success on the road. This game in Norman has already seen extensive ebb and flow with the oddsmakers and is considered a toss-up. My call is the Rebels, even with their 2-2 road record, as they keep their hopes alive for a fourth consecutive 10-win season and an outside shot at the CFP. Ole Miss is still Top 12 in the Futures Market for the national championship. X-Factor Player: Shekai Mills-Knight No. 33 has 33 carries this season for exactly 5 yards per carry!! With the terribly slow starts the Rebels' offense has experienced this year, I would fully expect to see SMK in the starting lineup against the Sooners. Bold Prediction: Ole Miss wins the old-fashioned way Oklahoma plays the lowest-scoring conference games in the SEC, averaging 41.3 combined points per contest. This Ole Miss team will certainly have its character tested in meat-grinder, smash-mouth fashion. The Ole Miss Rebels take on the Oklahoma Sooners at Gaylord Family – Oklahoma Memorial Stadium in Norman, Oklahoma, Saturday, Nov. 14th. Kickoff is currently set for 3:15 p.m. CT and will be broadcast on the SEC Network. Until then, follow along with The Rebel Walk for all the best coverage. away.blurb: It will be a high-pressure environment for Pete Golding's squad, and it looks like the Rebels will have to battle it out without their best offensive player. On Thursday, On3's Pete Nakos reported that Ole Miss' star running back Kewan Lacy is set to miss the remainder of the 2026 season due to his shoulder injury. The Ole Miss Rebels are 6-3 overall and 4-3 in SEC play after their brutal 42-7 loss to Georgia last weekend in Oxford. Two weeks before that, they fell 34-27 at Texas. Those are two ranked opponents who are firmly in the College Football Playoff Conversation, but it's too late in the season to be dropping games like that. Now they head into a crucial SEC clash at Oklahoma on Saturday, with the CFP potentially hanging in the balance. More news : Brian Kelly Sends Blunt Warning to Texas Ahead of LSU Clash Lacy quickly emerged as one of the best players in college football last season, rushing for 1,567 yards (third most in FBS) and 24 touchdowns (second) on an FBS-leading 306 attempts, averaging 5.1 yards per carry, along with 177 receiving yards. He earned first-team All-American and first-team All-SEC honors, and entered this year on the preseason watchlist for several national awards. But Lacy injured his left shoulder in the Rebels' loss to Texas on Oct. 24, and hasn't been able to recover. His third, and potentially final, college season ends after just six games, finishing with 388 rushing yards and five rushing touchdowns on 78 carries (5.0 yards per carry). Makhi Frazier, a Junior transfer from Michigan State, and sophomore Shekai Mills-Knight will continue to handle the bulk of the carries for Ole Miss. Frazier has 365 rushing yards on 72 carries this season (5.1 yards per carry), while Mills-Knight has 165 yards and three touchdowns on 33 carries (5.0 yards per carry).
