away.headline: Kewan Lacy Injury Update, Latest on Ole Miss Star's Status, Return Timeline amid CFP Bracket Push
away.blurb: Lacy missed time with a shoulder injury earlier this season before suffering a dislocated shoulder in an Oct. 24 game at Texas. He had already been ruled out of Saturday's matchup at Oklahoma. The running back was listed as the No. 21 prospect on Bleacher Report's 2027 NFL draft big board back in September. Lacy is eligible to either enter the draft or return for another college season in 2027. Saturday will mark Lacy's third straight absence. He will also be expected to sit out an Oct. 21 matchup against Wofford and the Oct. 27 regular-season finale against Mississippi State. Icon Sportswire/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images College Football Trinidad Chambliss and Ole Miss will have to continue their push for the College Football Playoff without star running back Kewan Lacy. On3's Pete Nakos reported Thursday Lacy is expected to miss the rest of the 2026 season due to injury. 10 Most Underrated Draft Prospects 🤫 Scouts have only gotten to see Lacy play the majority of a single college season. After appearing in six games as a true freshman at Missouri, Lacy joined Ole Miss in 2025 and went on to lead the FBS with 306 carries. Lacy paced the SEC with 24 rushing touchdowns during that sophomore season to go with 1,567 rushing yards over 15 games. Injuries have kept Lacy from replicating that campaign as a junior. He will finish the 2026 season with 78 carries for 388 yards and five scores. Lacy's injury issues started when he suffered what Ole Miss coach Pete Golding called a "bruised" left shoulder last December during a first-round CFP win over Tulane. He remained with the Rebels for the rest of their run to the CFP semifinals and later underwent offseason surgery on his shoulder. Lacy suffered a thigh injury in Ole Miss' season opener against Louisville, then rnjured his shoulder Sept. 19 against LSU. The running back missed one contest before returning to the lineup, only to suffer his next shoulder injury three games later. Ole Miss (6-3) fell nine spots to No. 19 in the second CFP selection committee rankings after a blowout loss to No. 2 Georgia last Saturday. That defeat left the Rebels with no room for error as Ole Miss works to convince the selection committee this team still deserves a playoff spot in Chambliss' last college season. away.headline: Injury Report: Ole Miss missing two offensive players against Oklahoma

Ole Miss coach Pete Golding confirmed his squad will be without two of its most important offensive players when the Rebels line up against the Sooners. Golding said running back Kewan Lacy and starting offensive lineman Patrick Kutas will miss the game. So far this season, the Sooners have typically had the least desirable injury report. But the two losses for Ole Miss are fairly significant, especially given the Rebels are coming off their third loss of the season. Golding said Kutas was injured in Ole Miss’ 42-7 loss at Georgia on Nov. 7. The Rebels will have to make adjustments across the offensive line. Former Sooner Troy Everett will likely replace Kutas at right guard as he did against Georgia. “Not season-ending,” Golding said of Kutas’ injury in his weekly presser. “Kutas got banged up pretty good, so we will not have Patrick this week. So there will be some moving parts to that and looking at some guys bumping inside. Golding later clarified Lacy will not play either. Against the Sooners last season, Lacy rushed 27 times for 78 yards and two touchdowns to help No. 8 Ole Miss defeat No. 13 Oklahoma 34–26. This season, however, he has missed a handful of games due to injury. Lacy missed the Georgia game, and it was a noticeable absence. Ole Miss (6-3, 4-3 SEC) mustered only 7 points against the Bulldogs. Lacy was a Doak Walker Award finalist last season. The honor is presented annually to the nation's top college football running back. He has run for five touchdowns this season but hasn’t seen the field since dislocating his shoulder against Texas in October. Ole Miss has lost two of the last three games in his absence. Oklahoma (5-4, 3-3 SEC) will have an opportunity to take advantage in Norman with kickoff scheduled for 3:15 p.m. CT. The game will be televised on the SEC Network. This is the third straight season the Sooners have played the Rebels and second straight season Oklahoma has hosted them. The league named the two schools annual rivals last season, meaning they'll play each other at home every season for at least the next four years. The Ole Miss Rebels are 6-3 overall and 4-3 in SEC play after their brutal 42-7 loss to Georgia last weekend in Oxford. Two weeks before that, they fell 34-27 at Texas. Those are two ranked opponents who are firmly in the College Football Playoff Conversation, but it's too late in the season to be dropping games like that. Now they head into a crucial SEC clash at Oklahoma on Saturday, with the CFP potentially hanging in the balance. He earned first-team All-American and first-team All-SEC honors, and entered this year on the preseason watchlist for several national awards. Ole Miss coach Pete Golding confirmed his squad will be without two of its most important offensive players when the Rebels line up against the Sooners. Golding said running back Kewan Lacy and starting offensive lineman Patrick Kutas will miss the game. So far this season, the Sooners have typically had the least desirable injury report. But the two losses for Ole Miss are fairly significant, especially given the Rebels are coming off their third loss of the season. Golding said Kutas was injured in Ole Miss’ 42-7 loss at Georgia on Nov. 7. The Rebels will have to make adjustments across the offensive line. Former Sooner Troy Everett will likely replace Kutas at right guard as he did against Georgia. “Not season-ending,” Golding said of Kutas’ injury in his weekly presser. “Kutas got banged up pretty good, so we will not have Patrick this week. So there will be some moving parts to that and looking at some guys bumping inside. Golding later clarified Lacy will not play either. Against the Sooners last season, Lacy rushed 27 times for 78 yards and two touchdowns to help No. 8 Ole Miss defeat No. 13 Oklahoma 34–26. This season, however, he has missed a handful of games due to injury. Lacy missed the Georgia game, and it was a noticeable absence. Ole Miss (6-3, 4-3 SEC) mustered only 7 points against the Bulldogs. Lacy was a Doak Walker Award finalist last season. The honor is presented annually to the nation's top college football running back. He has run for five touchdowns this season but hasn’t seen the field since dislocating his shoulder against Texas in October. Ole Miss has lost two of the last three games in his absence. Jon Sumrall returns to Kroger Field in Lexington, Ky., on Saturday, Nov. 14, at 6:15 p.m. ET (ESPN) when his Florida program takes on his alma mater, Kentucky. The Wildcats are 3.5-point home favorites, and my Florida vs. Kentucky prediction and college football picks expect Will Stein's team to win this game in the trenches. Who will win Florida vs Kentucky: Kentucky -3.5 After a hot September that had Florida ranked in the top 10 and climbing the college football national championship odds , the Gators have been one of the worst teams in the SEC. Since upsetting Ole Miss, Florida is 1-4 straight-up and against the spread, and their struggles will continue against Jon Sumrall's alma mater. I would take Kentucky to cover up to -4.5 . Florida is coming off its worst loss of the season, losing 23-17 at home to Oklahoma as a 3.5-point favorite, and switching back to Aaron Philo at QB won't save a team that's averaging 15.6 points per game since the start of October. The last time we saw Philo, he was benched in the World's Largest Outdoor Cocktail Party. Kentucky's defense isn't Georgia's, but it is disruptive enough to slow Florida down. The Wildcats rank 21st nationally in havoc rate (18.9%) and seventh in interceptions (12). TOP PICK Florida vs Kentucky Over/Under pick: Over 52.5 Florida's defense has been the death of it all season, and it hit an all-time low last week, making John Mateer look good. Kentucky's offense is far more efficient, and the reason I'd play the Over at 52.5 or better. The Wildcats have one of the best offensive lines in the country, paving the way for a unit ranked 16th nationally in success rate (49.2%) . With Kenny Minchey's efficiency (77.8% adjusted completion percentage) and the Wildcats' advantage on the line, they shouldn't have trouble converting on money downs against a defense sitting 132nd in third/fourth down success rate (54.8%). However, the Gators will move the ball too against a Kentucky defense that struggles to stop the run. The Wildcats are currently 96th in defensive success rate (45.8%), and Florida running back Jadan Baugh ranks top 10 nationally in forced missed tackles (48). Florida vs Kentucky combo During Florida's skid, its biggest issue has been slow starts. In its five games since the start of October, the Gators have trailed by 6+ points at halftime in each. Florida won and covered in just one of those games. If that trend continues, Kentucky should pull away in the second half, especially with Florida's defensive issues. Earlier in the season, the Gators could make up for the fact that their defense has one of the worst secondaries in the country, but since losing top wide receiver Vernell Brown III , they haven't been the same. The sophomore was averaging 3.87 yards per route run with zero drops; Florida's other starting receivers each have a drop rate of at least 7.7%. Brown hasn't played since the upset win over Ole Miss and is once again listed out on the SEC injury report . It's official: Poch to Man United Sportscaster Dan Hicks dies Story by Wildcats Wire Florida offense preview: Kentucky has to stop Jadan Baugh Braxton Howard, UK Wildcats Wire · Wildcats Wire Wed, November 11, 2026 at 6:24 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kentucky football failed the first test of this important November stretch, losing 34-6 to Tennessee . The Wildcats have to get off the mat quickly as they host the Florida Gators on Saturday night at Kroger Field. This is a Florida team that is reeling as they have lost four of their last five games. We will preview both sides of the football for the Gators, but we will start with their offense which is led by their star running back. Running back Jadan Baugh is essentially the entire Gators offense, he is the engine that makes it go. Similar to what we said about Tennessee's DeSean Bishop, but the Gators have struggled recently to get this run game going. That is the main reason they have lost four of their last five games. When you look at the win/loss splits of Baugh's stat line, it tells the whole story of Florida's offense. In the Gators' five wins this season, Baugh has rushed for 691 yards on 108 attempts for 12 rushing touchdowns and is averaging over six yards per carry in those wins. He has averaged 138 rushing yards per game in those five wins. Conversely, in Florida's four losses this season, Baugh has rushed for 145 yards on 52 attempts for 2 rushing touchdowns and is averaging under three yards per carry. He is averaging just 36 rushing yards per game in those losses. Teams have started to key in on the run game and slow Baugh down recently, as most of his success came in the first month of the season. In September when the Gators were rolling, Baugh had 600 rushing yards on 83 attempts and 11 of his 14 rushing touchdowns came in the first month of the season. He was averaging 150 rushing yards per game and over seven yards per carry in the month of September. Since then, Baugh has just 236 rushing yards on 77 attempts, averaging just 47 rushing yards per game and three yards per carry. It is simple for Kentucky's defense, stop this rushing attack led by Baugh and you will be in a great position to win this football game. Florida has a quarterback issue, as they have flipped back and forth between Aaron Philo and Tramell Jones. Philo was efficient in the first month of the season, but he dealt with an injury that allowed Jones to start in a big win on the road against Texas. Philo returned against Georgia, but a couple of boneheaded mistakes sent him to the bench. Jones completed 22-of-35 pass attempts for 155 passing yards and two touchdowns with no interceptions in the win over the Longhorns. Against Georgia and Oklahoma, the Gators only scored a total of 15 points. In those two losses, Jones completed 28-of-47 passes for 305 passing yards and no touchdown passes to three interceptions. Jones has thrown just four touchdown passes on the season and five interceptions. Philo on the other hand, has completed 70% of his passes this season for 1,367 yards for nine passing touchdowns. Philo also has five interceptions on the season. The biggest issue has been the injury of wide receiver Vernell Brown, who has not played in a game since the win over Ole Miss in September. Florida is struggling to generate any offense outside of the run game. This matchup is simple for Kentucky, they just have to key in and stop the run game for the Gators. Force Florida into a dropback heavy game, which will lead to turnover opportunities. Regardless if they start Philo or Jones, both have been turnover prone this season and the Gators are -3 in the turnover margin which ranks 98th among FBS teams. Kentucky's defense has to get stops early and play with a lead quickly. This article originally appeared on UK Wildcats Wire: Florida offense preview: Kentucky has to stop Jadan Baugh

away.headline: Oklahoma Sooners vs. Florida Gators: Final Injury Report for Week 10
away.blurb: It was a busy injury report week for the Sooners, but they'll have a few players available who had popped up on the report this week. Wide receivers Jer'Michael Carter and Elijah Thomas, tight end Rocky Beers, offensive lineman Jake Maikkula, defensive lineman Kenny Ozowalu, and defensive back Eli Bowen have been cleared to play against Florida. Two key players are game-time decisions against the Gators. Offensive lineman Eddy Pierre-Louis and defensive back Peyton Bowen still have their statuses up in the air as kickoff in The Swamp approaches. The Gators got some good news, as wide receiver Bailey Stockton and defensive lineman Emmanuel Oyebadejo are available for this game. Florida will be without wide receiver Vernell Brown III, tight end Evan Chieca, offensive lineman Emeka Ugorji, defensive lineman Jeremiah McCloud, and inside linebacker Jaden Robinson. For the Sooners, that means they'll have their full complement of skill-position players available Saturday night, except for Harris and Washington. The offensive line is still banged up without Fodje and possibly Pierre-Louis, the two projected starting guards coming into the year, but the five-man unit of Michael Fasusi, Noah Best, Maikkula, Heath Ozaeta, and E'Marion Harris is the healthiest the o-line has been in weeks. On game day, they are designated as available, game-time decision or out. • Out: Will not play, 0% chance to play. • Doubtful: Unlikely to play, 25% chance to play. • Questionable: Uncertain to play, 50% chance to play. • Probable: Probable to play, 75% chance to play. No. 16 Tennessee football heads into its the final month of the regular season relatively healthy, beginning with a pivotal game against No. 7 Kentucky on Nov. 7. The Vols listed no new injured players on the final SEC student-athlete availability report, which was released 90 minutes before kickoff. Tennessee (6-2, 3-2 SEC) plays Kentucky (7-1, 5-1) at 6:15 p.m. ET at Neyland Stadium for its Dark Mode game . It will be broadcast on ESPN. The Vols healed up during their off week. But that was only after being plagued by a string of serious injuries early in the season. Seven Tennessee players have already suffered season-ending injuries in 2026: starting left guard Wendell Moe ; starting safety Edrees Farooq (knee); starting tight end Ethan Davis (knee); safety Dylan Lewis (foot); wide receiver/kick returner Joakim Dodson (leg); linebacker Jaedon Harmon (knee); and cornerback Jadais Richard (upper-body). Tennessee football injury report Kentucky football injury report How SEC availability report works The SEC student-athlete availability report was introduced in the 2024 season for conference games only. The initial report is released on Wednesday of an SEC game week, with daily updates leading to a final report 90 minutes prior to kickoff of a Saturday game. Here’s what those designations mean: Per SEC policy, schools must accurately designate players’ participation status. If the school has knowledge that a player may not be able to participate in the upcoming game for any reason (injury, illness, suspension, ineligibility or personal matter), it must report it. Failure to do so will subject schools to potential penalties ranging from $25,000 for a first offense to $100,000 for a third and further offenses. Now, the Cardinals will quickly turn their attention to their second straight road game, as Jeff Brohm and Louisville will face Bill Belichick and the North Carolina Tar Heels. UNC is currently sitting in 9th place in the ACC with a 5-4 record, but the Tar Heels are a team that can’t be taken lightly as they have played Notre Dame and Miami very closely. Now, UofL will try to earn its fifth straight win and seventh win of the season. This marks the Cardinals' fourth road game of the season, with Louisville currently 2-1, including wins over Syracuse and Georgia Tech. The Utes are ranked No. 2 in the latest CFP poll as one of two undefeated teams remaining. After beating their hated rivals BYU last week, Utah's path to the Playoff -- and the Big 12 title game -- is clear, but they must turn the page quickly from taking down the Cougars as a trip to Tucson could prove tricky. Arizona climbed to No. 23 in this week's rankings after beating TCU in a thriller, and the 7-2 Wildcats' only losses this season have been to the other top teams in the Big 12 -- BYU and Texas Tech . Both of those losses came on the road, and Arizona will be relishing the opportunity to prove they belong in the top tier of the Big 12 when they finally get to welcome one of the big boys to southern Arizona. For the Utes, a win writes their name into the CFP bracket in pencil, as they'd improve to 10-0 with two games left where they'd be heavy favorites over TCU and West Virginia . The Wildcats, meanwhile, can pick up the biggest win of Brent Brennan's tenure and solidify their place in the Big 12's upper tier. Utah vs. Arizona: Need to know Refocusing the Utes: The Utes put everything they had into winning The Holy War last week against BYU, in the first-ever matchup between the rivals while both were ranked in the top 10. It was obvious how much they put into the game plan with their hot start, and then they were forced to dig deep and rally after the Cougars answered with some haymakers of their own. That win was a proof point for Morgan Scalley in his first season as head coach, but this week might show us more about the kind of culture he's building in Salt Lake City. There's a natural urge to exhale after that kind of win, but Arizona is going to be juiced up for the chance to face the No. 2 team in the country at home. The Utes have to find a way to match that energy -- or at least withstand an early onslaught -- and get the game back on their terms. Strength on strength in the pass game: Arizona is one of the best passing offenses in the country with veteran quarterback Noah Fifita who is both efficient with a 73% completion rate and dynamic with 23 pass plays of 30-plus yards -- third-most in the country. Fifita and his favorite target Isaiah Mizell can take the lid off of most defenses and apply constant stress -- especially with Fifita's ability to extend plays and get outside the pocket. However, they'll be going up against one of the nation's best pass defenses that had Bear Bachmeier completely lost a week ago. Utah is allowing opposing quarterbacks to complete just 51.3% of passes (2nd lowest in the country) and is tied for fourth in interceptions with 13 (including four last week). The Utes pass defense is hyper aggressive, and they have four players with two or more interceptions this season. If there is one weakness to the Utah defense, it is that they have been susceptible to big plays in the passing game. The Utes have allowed 15 pass plays of 30+ yards this season, which ranks 104th in the country. Fifita and Arizona will have to take advantage of those opportunities for chunk plays when they present themselves because moving the ball consistently against the Utes is incredibly difficult. Arizona's pass rush vs. Devon Dampier : The Utes defense will get plenty of attention, but Arizona hasn't been a slouch on that side of the ball this year either. The strength of their defense is their pass rush, which is 10th in the nation in sacks per game (3.11). Devon Dampier is a tough quarterback to wrangle with his combination of strength and elusiveness, but the Wildcats are going to try to heat up Dampier to create some negative plays or, more ideally, turnovers. How Utah's offensive line handles Arizona's rush and how Dampier manages plays when the Wildcats do get pressure on him will be critical in this game. Utah has allowed just 13 sacks this season, thanks to a quality offensive line and Dampier's escapability, but that will be put to the test against the Wildcats. If Arizona is going to win this game, they need to find ways to get the Utes' offense behind the sticks and probably need to win the turnover battle. The pass rush is going to be their best weapon to accomplish both of those goals, and if Arizona is going to pull off the upset, expect the pass rush to be leading the charge. That said, so far this season, when Arizona has played the best teams in the Big 12, it has proven to be lagging just a bit behind. Over 60 minutes, I expect that to be the case again on Saturday, even with a raucous environment in Tucson for their biggest home game in years. Utah won't have it easy, but when the clock hits triple zeroes, I expect the Utes to move to 10-0 and cover the short number. Getting to the Big 12 Championship isn't out of the question, but losses to BYU and Texas Tech make that hard. However, take down the unbeaten and No. 2 team, and watch the Cats rocket up the rankings. Or , Utah could come up with a terrific ranked win on the road, and at 10-0, it would all but lock up a spot in the CFP. Utah has a sneaky-tough date at TCU after this before finishing with a sneaky-nasty game against a high-powered West Virginia. They can hit the deep shots and be explosive, but they're at their best when quarterback Devon Dampier and the running game go on long marches. Utah keeps the ball a Big 12-best 32:50 a game, but … Why Arizona Will Win Arizona can match the Utes when it comes to tempo. Utah is No. 1 in the conference in time of possession, but Arizona holds the ball for well over 32 minutes, quarterback Noah Fifita is great at hitting short-range third-down throws, and the defense is usually a killer against the run. This isn't necessarily a ball-hawking Wildcat defense, but it's been better at taking the ball away with six over the last four games. Utah has turned it over twice in each ofthe last five games. Texas Tech ripped off 320 yards, West Virginia ran for over 300, and BYU averaged close to five yards per carry – the Wildcats lost to the Red Raiders and Cougars. Utah runs well, and it'll get a few gashing runs, but it was held in check by Colorado in Boulder, and didn't run all that well against BYU last week. But here's Utah's biggest problem – the Arizona pass rush. Dampier can move and make plays, but he and the Utah backfield get hit behind the line too often. The other issue for the Utes is a lack of pass rush that should bother Fifita enough to matter in key moments late. Arizona will survive, helped by a +2 turnover margin. picks.blurb: Utah Utes expert previews the Arizona Wildcats football game, makes a score prediction | Arizona Desert Swarm Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo An Arizona Wildcats Community Arizona Desert Swarm November 13, 2026 Arizona Desert Swarm Notifications Notifications The Feed Sections Arizona Basketball Arizona Football Arizona Softball Arizona Recruiting Arizona Soccer Arizona Volleyball Arizona Baseball Arizona Gymnastics Arizona in the Pros Betting Betting News FanDuel College Football Odds FanDuel College Basketball Odds Arizona Football Odds Arizona Basketball Odds College Football Picks and Predictions College Basketball Picks and Predictions Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Sections Expand Arizona Basketball Betting Expand Betting News Community Guidelines All communities Notifications Arizona Football During their decade-plus together in the Pac-12, Arizona and Utah had plenty of great battles, but the results tended to be streaky. The Wildcats won four straight meetings from 2012-15, then Utah took six in a row before the UA claimed the last two, including their Big 12 debut in 2024 when it beat a Top 10 Utes squad on the road. But the opponent coming to Tucson this weekend is better than any of those previous versions. Utah is 9-0 and ranked No. 2 nationally, one of two unbeaten teams in FBS. To better understand the Utes, we reached out to Josh Furlong of KSL.com for some insight and a score prediction. Below are his spirited answers to our lifeless questions: AZ Desert Swarm: What have been the main keys to Utah getting off to its best start since 2008? Josh Furlong: “The easy answer is quarterback Devon Dampier, who has been healthy and efficient as the team’s biggest playmaker, but it ultimately comes down to the culture Morgan Scalley has built at Utah in such a short time. He’s allowing the players to be loose while focused, understanding that it takes each person to contribute to wins. He’s an extremely competitive coach, but he’s able to pair that with a system that allows players to make mistakes, grow and develop.” Arizona fans still have nightmares about Devon Dampier from two years ago at New Mexico, and he seems to have only gotten better. Where has his game most improved this season, and is there anything he still struggles with? “Dampier has worked on going through his progressions and staying in the pocket more, which has allowed Utah to do more with him at QB. It’s giving him more structure while understanding that he still needs room to freelance and be the dynamic QB he can be. All of that has allowed him to have more confidence, especially now that he’s been paired with a better group of wide receivers. At times, though, he gets happy feet and doesn’t have the right mechanics in his throws, which can sometimes limit his passing.” Wayshawn Parker apparently got banged up against BYU but should be good to go for this game. What does he bring to the offense when healthy? “Wayshawn Parker simply opens up the options for Utah’s offense. His threat as a runner, especially as he breaks through tackles, makes him one of the top offensive names you have to take away. But by doing so, opposing defenses have to handle many other players that can be just as effective in advancing the offense — Dampier, Daniel Bray, Byrd Ficklin, Braden Pegan, Creed Whittemore, etc. On top of that, he’s really developed a great pass blocking game, which has been a huge advantage in keeping Dampier upright and doing what he does.” Arizona’s secondary has been dealing with injuries and got exploited a bit last week with deep passes. Who would be the beneficiaries of this in the Ute receiving corps? “The primary receiving target would be Braden Pegan (WR1), who is a multi-faceted receiver who can do pretty much anything needed, and is paired with Ricky Johnson and Creed Whittemore. Johnson is a smooth runner with great separation and great hands. Whittemore works primarily in the slot and has been great in the intermediate game, especially with opposing defenses focusing on Pegan and the potential run threats of Dampier, Ficklin, Parker. Another option is tight end Noah Bennee, who is the benefactor of all the other skills players being the top of mind. As the defense focuses on other players, Bennee sneaks out and can be a problem with his size.” How do you expect Utah to defend Arizona’s passing attack? “Utah will primarily operate in man coverage and force Noah Fifita to beat them one-on-one, while the defensive coordinator Colton Swan schemes up disguises and blitzes to keep Fifita uncomfortable. Because Fifita is so explosive, it’s likely Utah will try more contain while pressuring him.” Morgan Scalley had been the coach in waiting at Utah for a while, and we’re seeing why with this 9-0 start. What are the biggest differences between him and Kyle Whittingham? “The biggest difference is that Scalley is a people’s person. Kyle Whittingham cared more about coaching football and not the other elements, whereas Scalley sees it all interconnected. He shares the same hard-nosed, physical approach of Whittingham but wants a connected team that has no factions. It’s not, offense gets to know offense and defense gets to know defense, it’s a team-wide look as each works to understand the other. He’s also open to feedback, assuming that the feedback actually is presented in a way that helps change and it’s just complaining, though he’d listen to anyone who is frustrated. He wants all to feel connected and bought into the program, regardless of their standing with the team.” Prediction time. Does Utah move one step closer to an unbeaten regular season or does Arizona pull off a November upset at home and stay in the hunt for the Big 12 title game and the playoffs? Give us a score pick. “This game in Tucson is always a tricky one. Even when Utah has been the clear favorite, it’s far from a decisive win for the Utes. I think Scalley has his squad more focused on this game than it might have been in year’s past, which leads me to believe Utah will be ready for any blow and not be caught off guard in a road environment. I think Utah is the more complete team, but they’ve got to stop Fifita. To me, Utah wins this game if they can contain Fifita (as much as possible) and cannot give up momentum to an opposing crowd. I see Utah winning something like 31-24 .” Download the new SB Nation app All of your communities in one place. College Football 27 prediction: UA 26, Utah 21 Arizona took a 23-14 lead in the early moments of the fourth quarter following a 51-yard field goal by kicker Michael Salgado-Medina, who made two field goals earlier in the game. Salgado-Medina made his fourth field goal on Arizona's second-to-last drive of the game and the Wildcats led 26-14. Arizona wide receiver Isaiah Mizell had six catches for 100 yards and two touchdowns, including a 56-yard score on a slant route on fourth-and-2 on Arizona's opening drive. Despite Utah getting within a possession, Arizona picked up three first downs on its final drive and forced Utah to burn all of its timeouts. After Arizona punter Chase Ridley pinned the Utes on the 1-yard line, Utah had 30 seconds to go to the length of the field. Utah ran out of time. Wildcats win. home.headline: Colorado Loses Two Defenders in Latest Injury Report Before Arizona State
home.blurb: The Colorado Buffaloes have had very few bounces go their way in terms of injuries this season, but they were hopeful that may change in Week 10. The Buffaloes had a few players who weren’t ruled out for the majority of the week, and although they were battling injuries, there was still some hope they may play against the Arizona State Sun Devils. However, Friday’s update was the bearer of bad news for Colorado fans. All but one of those players were ruled out, and the final member of that list’s status is still undetermined. Thankfully for Colorado, the two members of the injury report who were listed as probable will play. Those two were cornerback Cree Thomas and Sean Kinney. Namely, Kinney has been an impact player for the entire season since winning Colorado’s starting center job. Backup Demetrius Hunter went down with a likely season-ending injury in Week 1, and Kinney hasn’t wavered in his increased snap count. As of Thursday, Taufatofua and Mitchell still had a chance to play, though they were listed as doubtful. However, Friday’s report officially ruled them out. Mitchell has been an anchor in the Buffaloes’ secondary, as he and fellow safety Randon Fontenette have been the most dependable part of that unit. As for Taufatofua, he’s been dealt a bad hand with injuries this season, as he missed Colorado’s first four games as well. But when he made his return against the then-No. 12 Texas Tech Red Raiders in Week 5, he was a solid contributor right away. He assisted Santana Hopper in creating pressure as a hybrid defensive lineman, and Hopper likely wouldn’t have had the game he did without him. There was also hope that Welch could return this week , but that was shut down with the week’s first injury report. In addition, Scudero, who played in the first two games of the season, still hasn't returned from the injury report. His chances of playing again this season continue to get slimmer by the week. But those unfortunate updates go to show the type of luck Colorado has had with injuries this season. Manuel is the lone player from the Buffs’ midweek injury reports who still has a chance to play against ASU. He was upgraded to questionable on Thursday, and that status remained on Friday’s report. Defensive lineman Vili Taufatofua But before Taufatofua could build much momentum off of a few solid performances, he finds himself back on the injury report. He missed Colorado’s game against the Kansas State Wildcats in Week 9 and will now miss a second-straight against the Sun Devils. Manuel has been crucial to the interior of the Buffs’ defensive line this season, and Colorado will have a taller task in front of it when trying to stop ASU’s rushing attack if he can’t go. Luckily for the Buffaloes, they have depth on the interior defensive line, but Manuel’s absence is still one they hope to avoid. Andre Cojoe has given up almost twice the pressure that Goosby did, necessitating a move to right tackle almost immediately, while Melvin Siani has had struggles on the blindside in Goosby's stead. It's been rough sledding since Goosby went down in the first quarter against the Ole Miss Rebels in Week 8. Blake Baker's defensive schemes have boosted LSU's talent up front this season. The Tigers have one of the best pass rushes in the SEC, with three different players having at least five sacks through the first nine games of the season. LSU defensive end Princewill Umanmielen leads the defense with 8.5 sacks, while Jordan Ross has five sacks, three pass deflections, and a 30-yard pick six as the cherry on top. Meanwhile, in the middle, Deuce Geralds has been a force through the A-gap. Geralds has five sacks and has caught up to speed against the run. UT may not have a tougher test all season than this defensive front. It makes it even harder when you account for Manning and Steve Sarkisian's communication issues against a Tiger Stadium crowd at night. We'll see if Kyle Flood's group has the chops to keep it together for the offensive skill-position players behind them in Death Valley during a major matchup for the CFP's sake. On his Always College Football Week 11 preview , McElroy picked LSU to win 24-20 and called the Tigers’ pass rush against Texas’ protection “probably the most lopsided matchup on the board” on a slate with four games between ranked playoff teams. Why does McElroy trust LSU? Texas (7-2) is coming off a 34-20 win at Missouri in which Manning threw for 297 yards and three touchdowns, but he still went down three times. McElroy pointed to the quarterback’s patience as part of the problem. “He does hold the ball looking for the perfect throw, and behind that line, the perfect throw sometimes arrives after the defense arrives,” McElroy said. Edge rusher Princewill Umanmielen, an Austin native who followed Kiffin from Ole Miss, is the player McElroy expects to attack a Texas line that has struggled with twists and stunts. The Longhorns also listed offensive lineman Trevor Goosby as out on their availability report for the Missouri game. McElroy said three LSU sacks would leave Texas “in third-and-long, where it converts just 20% of the time.” Sam Leavitt and LSU’s red zone LSU Tigers Quarterback Sam Leavitt | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect LSU (6-3) brings flaws of its own after a 31-13 home loss to Alabama. Sam Leavitt completed 35 of 47 passes for 380 yards, but the Tigers went 0-for-4 on fourth down and scored one touchdown on four red zone trips. “I wouldn’t think that would equal 13 points ,” Kiffin said afterward. Alabama’s fourth-quarter surge in Baton Rouge led Booger McFarland to declare the Crimson Tide a playoff lock , and Texas brings a defense built to repeat that formula. The Longhorns rank first nationally in adjusted defensive EPA per play, according to Game on Paper . “Texas’ defense is good enough to hold LSU to field goals, which is why I think this stays a fight,” McElroy said. LSU’s tempo is the Tigers’ counter. McElroy noted that LSU runs nearly 80 plays per game and said, “If LSU’s tempo has the Texas linebackers gassed by, say, the fourth quarter, then the best defense on the field stops being the best defense on the field.” What’s at stake in Baton Rouge? McElroy said a fourth loss would make LSU’s playoff chances “a no-go,” while a win would put the Tigers “back in the playoff mix.” The New Orleans native grew up attending LSU games, but Steve Sarkisian doesn’t expect the homecoming to distract his quarterback. “I don’t think he gives a crap, I’ll be honest with you,” Sarkisian said. “I really think he’s thinking about what coverages they’re going to play .” Kiffin, who recruited Manning at Ole Miss, offered praise with one exception. “I think he’s an awesome kid and I hope he does really well, obviously outside of Saturday,” Kiffin said. Hutson, who struggled through a lengthy eligibility case this offseason, officially returned to the Horns' roster just before the season kicked off, but has played fewer than 10 snaps all year. So, while having the additional depth, much less depth with so much experience, is always great, the possibility of his absence on Saturday should not raise any red flags for Longhorns Nation. home.headline: Cole Hutson popping up on Texas's injury report vs. LSU shouldn't raise any red flags
home.blurb: Of course, Hutson was only listed as "questionable," so there is still a chance that he would be available for the additional depth. OUT: Hollywood Smothers (RB), Trevor Goosby (OL), Nick Townsend (TE), Richard Wesley (EDGE) Goosby is the only other offensive lineman on the availability report and has been sidelined with a torn patellar tendon and the subsequent reparative surgery. Similarly, Texas running back Hollywood Smothers has been ruled out for the remainder of the season with a torn MCL. The best news from the report was the update to defensive tackle Hero Kanu's status, upgrading him from questionable to probable. Both tight end Nick Townsend and edge rusher Richard Wesley are still labeled as "out," with Wesley having been sidelined since the Horns' game against the Florida Gators. Townsend has been on and off the availability report, but most recently took the field against the Mississippi State Bulldogs. While Hutson's addition to the report wasn't ideal, Texas's availability report was actually good news for the Horns, as was the second report out of Baton Rouge. OUT: Dashawn Spears (S), Phillip Wright III (WR), Charles Ross II (LB), Richard Anderson (DT) Then, the impending return of LSU star linebacker Whit Weeks could wreak even more havoc on the Horns' offense, but he was listed as questionable by head coach Lane Kiffin for a second time this week. A final availability report will come out on Friday evening at 7:10 p.m. CT. Then, No. 7 Texas and No. 21 LSU are scheduled to kick off at 6:30 p.m. CT on Saturday, Nov. 14, and the game will be broadcast on ABC. While the last thing you want is any player on an injury list, the surprise presence of Texas offensive lineman Cole Hutson on the Longhorns' latest availability report should not raise any concerns as they prepare to face the LSU Tigers. Hutson, who struggled through a lengthy eligibility case this offseason, officially returned to the Horns' roster just before the season kicked off, but has played fewer than 10 snaps all year. So, while having the additional depth, much less depth with so much experience, is always great, the possibility of his absence on Saturday should not raise any red flags for Longhorns Nation. Even with how shaky the Texas O-Line has been at protecting quarterback Arch Manning, Hutson has not even been taking the field alongside the rest of the offensive linemen like center Connor Robertson or now-sidelined left tackle Trevor Goosby. Reliford hasn't seen the field since September, but has 18 total career tackles (six solo) and 0.5 sacks. home.headline: SEC releases initial injury report for Texas at LSU
home.blurb: Texas defensive tackle Hero Kanu suffered an injury against Missoui, but reporting indicates that he may still give it a go against LSU, which puts his listing of questionable at odds with the reporting out there this week. On the LSU side of things, starting linebacker Whit Weeks is questionable after missing several weeks with a leg injury that he suffered against Texas A&M back in September. There is a chance that he could be back on the field come Saturday, and would be a significant addition to the starting lineup for the Tigers. Starting offensive tackle Weston Davis has been designated as probable, which means he will more than likely be a full go on Saturday after getting dinged up against Alabama this past week.
